comments.author: Raj Abhijit Dandekar
comments.comment: Skipping the coding test is a smart filter, but the real tell is whether someone can debug a bad agent run, not just demo a clean one. Teaching the transformer on a whiteboard exposes mental models faster than syntax checks. What failure mode do you screen for first, tool misuse or weak stopping criteria? #AgenticAI

comments.author: Natan Mohart
comments.comment:
A lot of AI features just move work from writing to checking. If an AI note can't show the exact source span it used, I treat it as a polished guess. What's the minimum trust signal that makes an AI feature worth keeping?

#AI #Product #Engineering

comments.author: Louis Graffeuil
comments.comment: 75% of these repos are under a year old, so the bottleneck is not discovery, it is evaluation. I only keep skills that measurably reduce human edits, not just generate more plausible code. Which two actually changed your merge rate?

comments.author: Michael Hofer
comments.comment: I treat long-running agent drift like model drift: version the prompt, tools, memory schema, and run weekly regression evals on real transcripts. The failure mode I see most is not a bad answer, it’s the agent trusting a stale context that used to be true. How are you detecting that kind of quiet decay in production? #AIAgents #Evals #LLMs

comments.author: Benoit Baylin
comments.comment:
Cross checking outputs is useful, but the bigger win is a shared context layer. If Claude, Codex, and your agents read and write the same wiki, you stop reexplaining the business on every run. What broke first when multiple agents started sharing one knowledge base?

#AIEngineering #Agents #MCP
